title: Favorite banjo players in New Orleans
summary: Asked about banjo players he admired, Hamilton names a Marrero and the fast Poise Sevier; he never took up guitar.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Who were the best banjo players here in New Orleans when you were young, when you were a kid, even before you took it up? Can you, anybody that you watched or liked?
Well it was a fella, there were two fellas that I know, one of them was one of those Marrero, but it wasn't Lawrence.

It wasn't John Marrero. I used to call him Ruth Gordon, and yeah, him. And there was another fella, oh he was fast, and he was a younger boy, he was wild. I mean, I think he was a sincere, Poise Sevier. Poise Sevier, yeah, I've heard George Williams about him. Poise Sevier, yeah, oh he was just fast, he was fast as lightning. But he had a different style in those fellas, and I had met him in Natchez later, years after I left here. But those were about the two, well I never did pay much attention to banjo players much during in them days. Did you ever play guitar, by the way?
Did you ever take up the guitar? No, I never take up the guitar.
